San José's declared process never mentions the 15-business-day written completeness determination, the 60-day ministerial clock, the deemed-complete/deemed-approved backstops, or the appeal right — all four are mandated by Gov. Code § 66317. This is the model's central availability gap, not an omission in the gold.
San José's process page ends at 'your ADU is ready for moving in!' and never mentions the Certificate of Occupancy that Gov. Code § 66328 requires before occupancy (D8).

No ADU fee amount is published anywhere in Wave 1 except the $398/hour preliminary-meeting rate. The five Issuance-Review fee components (residual plan review, inspection, building permit application, school, parkland) are named but never priced, so fee error is unscoreable for San José.
The PowerBI dashboards (D4) are the observed tier and their underlying numbers were not extracted; only D5's narrative counts survive.
Why ADU permit issuance fell 10% from 2024 to 2025 is stated but unexplained; D5 offers only a generic reference to state-law compliance and 'permit process enhancements'.

Nothing describes how the Prescreen Review decides an application is 'ready for plan review' — i.e. San José's operative completeness criteria — beyond 'City staff will NOT process inaccurate or incomplete plans!'
Whether and how the § 66317(a)(3) tolling and bundled-new-primary-dwelling provisions are invoked in practice is unknown.

The ADU Service appointment track (linked from D1's sidebar as 'ADU Service' under Building Permit Services) was not captured in Wave 1; it is the track D3 excludes, so the single most relevant timing document is missing.

D1 and D2 are Wayback-sourced markdown; inline link syntax and ** bold markers interrupt several sentences in the saved .txt, so some quotes here are deliberately short fragments that are contiguous in the source.

Disentanglement boundary: AB 2533 amnesty legalisation of a pre-2020 unpermitted unit is a separate track (HCD itself lists AB 2533 as a distinct entry; LADBS runs a separate SOP for it). A solver that mixes amnesty steps into this model has made a disentanglement error.
notes: Why San José is the strongest ADU gold: its own program page publishes what is functionally a back-office routing sequence — the three-phase SJePlans pipeline of Prescreen Review → Plan Review → Issuance Review, with the fee split across two of the three phases — and its Legistar record supplies both observed permit counts and the affordability-imputation methodology behind them. The five staff_only activities split into two kinds. Two are per-case and invisible: the assignment of a Supervising Planner (A19), which leaks only from a mailing instruction on one optional JADU form, and the internal sequencing and due-dating of the concurrent building and fire reviews (A12), whose parameters are unpublished for ADUs specifically because D3 excludes the ADU track. Three are downstream of the applicant entirely: the affordability survey (A29) and the ABAG-methodology imputation and HCD filing (A30) mean every ADU permit is silently counted into a state report and assigned an affordability level the owner never stated. The gold's most useful property for ceiling measurement is a clean four-way absence: the statute mandates a 15-business-day completeness notice, a 60-day decision, two deemed-approval backstops and an appeal route, and San José's declared footprint mentions none of them (A10, A13, A27, A28). A solver working from declared_only can reconstruct San José's pipeline in fine detail and still miss every enforceable clock — exactly the availability term this benchmark is built to isolate. gold_tier is 'designed+observed': the process model is designed-tier, while the 2025 permit and application counts in D5 and the volume dashboards in D4 are records-derived.
